question.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ onto the plane $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v}+t\mathbf{w},$ where $s,t\in\mathbb R,$ and
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117156/assets/c7b322970113e415b78a9cc74469c6cad86404f0929e2091f8c6be2e1329f7bf.svg)
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S} \: \mathbf{x} = A\left(A^T\!A\right)^{-1}\!A^T\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3.$ In our case, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117156/assets/736da2e7e8541700ba158e3b983bc2320427755eb7da3190b62dc743972d083c.svg)
Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}12 & 4 \\ 4 & 12\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{32}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
